title: Phye ghan (wind bell)
summary: A small iron bell hangs from a bamboo beam outside a hill house. A flat wooden paddle hangs inside it, and when the wind moves the paddle, it knocks the bell and rings.
howToPlay: Four places are lit: Lip, Waist, Shoulder and Paddle.
Strike the place a closing ring marks.
Let each ring fade before the next, like a breeze.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: A bell whose clapper is moved by the wind rather than by a hand rings out over the terraces (the picture shows it enlarged).
credits: Tradition: the wind bell of the Sunuwar people; patterns written for this game
